text:
elaine: heads-up — ap-southeast1 gpu-pool-3 queue depth jumped ~3x over the last 6m, majority of requests are for mosaic-clarity-7b. tail latency and eviction churn visible in pod logs. spilling into shared-low-priority pool.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT ap-southeast1/gpu-pool-3 queue_depth=312 threshold=100 pod_evictions=18 in 10m. top model: mosaic-clarity-7b (68% of queued tokens). link: https://observability/redwood/ap-southeast1/pool-3

sam: who is oncall for infra right now?

kari: i'm oncall, looking at grafana now. tail p95 jumping to ~2.4s for generation_token time; CPU on host nodes not high, GPU utilization ~92% with frequent context-switches.

elaine: looks like kv-cache thrash — many short requests with different prefixes. cache miss rate for clarity-7b up to 65%.

navid: two quick mitigation options: warm a tiny dedicated pool for clarity-7b (4 smaller gpus) or enforce per-model RPS cap to throttle best-effort traffic. warm pool reduces latency but costs ~$320/day in our estimates.

kari: can we do a cheap rate cap first then spin warm pool if it persists?

sam: agree. also consider token-length based admission: block bursts >512 tokens for now — most heavy jobs are long tail batch jobs from batch-inference tenants.

elaine: ok i'll set a soft per-model cap and enable KV cache persistence flag for clarity-7b to reduce misses. planning: 
```# runtime CLI
redwood route set-rate-limit --region ap-southeast1 --model mosaic-clarity-7b --rps 14 --burst 28
redwood runtime set-config --model mosaic-clarity-7b --kv_cache.persist=true
```

navid: i'll start the warm pool prep in parallel (ami bake + scheduling profile). ETA ~18m to have 4 ready and warm. i'll also add a fallback mapping for non-SLAd customers to mosaic-clarity-3b.

ops-bot: executed quick fallback patch for non-critical customers: route-fallback-ap-southeast1.json applied. affected routes: /embed-bulk non-sla -> mosaic-clarity-3b.

kari: monitoring: created a short-lived dashboard and synthetic test to validate latency for clarity-7b and fallback traffic. alert on p95 > 1.8s or queue_depth > 150.

sam: cost callout — warm pool + higher RPS = cost spike. can we set dynamic scale-down after 60m of stable metrics?

navid: yes. warm pool autoscale policy: scale-to-0-after 60m idle. manual kill if not needed.

elaine: immediate plan of record: 1) apply per-model RPS cap (i'm doing it now). 2) enable kv_cache.persist (i'll push). 3) navid to spin warm pool and apply fallback mapping for non-SLA. 4) kari to watch dashboard and escalate if p95 stays >1.8s after 30m. 5) cost owner to review tomorrow for root-cause work (cache-friendly runtime change or model quantization).

sam: assigning owners: elaine (rate + kv), navid (warm pool + fallback), kari (monitoring). I'll follow up with incident summary after stabilization.

ops-bot: action logs: rate-limit applied by elaine at 1712350022, kv_cache.persist toggled at 1712350058, fallback mapping applied by navid at 1712350104.

kari: initial numbers after changes: queue_depth fell from 312 -> 130 in ~7m, p95 down from 2.4s -> 1.6s. still watching for spillover.

elaine: thanks team. will keep thread updated — next step: triage root cause (cache size, token distribution, or model behavior) and propose permanent mitigation (warm pools for high-qps models or per-tenant fairshare). :thumbsup:
